## Teaching

::: {.teaching-item}
### Survey Sampling

**ENSEA, Abidjan · Semester 2 · 2026–2027 · 25 hours · 2.5 credits**

This course develops the methodological foundations needed to design sample
surveys while accounting for the practical constraints of fieldwork, prior
information, and the study setting.

The syllabus covers:

- survey design, data-collection methods, and sources of survey error (2 hours);
- simple random sampling, estimation, precision, and sample selection (5 hours);
- non-probability methods, including quota, route, typical-unit, and volunteer sampling (6 hours); and
- designs using auxiliary information: unequal probabilities, stratification,
  multistage sampling, and cluster sampling (12 hours).

Assessment is based on one written examination.
:::

### Books, talks & explainers

- [Causality for the Brave and True](https://matheusfacure.github.io/python-causality-handbook/landing-page.html), a practical causal-inference handbook.
- [Econimate](https://t.co/5O0ziYSjJy), animated explanations of economics research.
- [Public speaking for academic economists](https://gouvci-my.sharepoint.com/:b:/g/personal/j_migone_stat_plan_gouv_ci/EbLOkKzRI5tNs2JG9tTGwFoBXj5IbXdcpepUSA_MRmcjjg?e=8mnZ5F), by Rachael Meager.
- [Microsimulating the impact of public policies on households](https://gouvci-my.sharepoint.com/:b:/g/personal/j_migone_stat_plan_gouv_ci/EbLOkKzRI5tNs2JG9tTGwFoBXj5IbXdcpepUSA_MRmcjjg?e=YH6Qcw) (in French).
